questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: As a vibrant student city, Boston is home to numerous prestigious universities. Further, Boston University is especially known for its welcoming environment for international students. The city's European feel eases the transition from Denmark, reducing culture shock. Additionally, Boston is bike- and walk-friendly, making it convenient to navigate and explore. Lastly, I had never been to the east coast of United States before.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy to find the information I needed upon arrival. Boston University was very helpful in providing the necessary resources and guidance for a smooth transition.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Upon arrival, we received assistance from staff who helped us check into our housing accommodation. Additionally, there were two orientation days—one general and one specifically for exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
Apartments: Single room in an apartment (1 person, 2 person or 4 person apartments). Double room in an apartment. Bathroom shared with few others. 

Doorms: Double, triple, quad room. Bathroom shared with up to 20 others. 

Suites: Single or double rooms. Bathroom shared with less than 8 others.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Dining plans with three central primary dining halls on campus. Also cooking facilities if you get an on campus apartment. Highly recommend anyone getting a dining plan though for the social experience of dining with other American or international students.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It's expensive and it's kind of a lottery what you get from your prioritizations. However, I got lucky and got what I requested - an apartment on campus which I shared with three other Americans. I had a single room as well. I think there are a lot of good different options, so don't worry too much. Also, a few of my friends managed to change their accommodation by talking to BU housing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We could register a few months before from Denmark. It was just through StudentLink and it was kind of easy. Further, everyone has the option to change courses in the first two weeks - called "shopping week".

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could read about the different courses online - that was it concerning the course content. However, we got a good introduction about how to register at StudentLink from our exchange administrator.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted. However, exchange students gets to choose courses after regular students - so a good amount of courses were already full when I got the chance to regsister.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be flexible and don't panic if you don't get the courses you want straight away. Often, American students overload the first week and then drop courses they don't want - so just keep an eye on StudentLink in the first week and you will be good.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: On average, the course levels were similar to Denmark.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: We were fewer students so you really had to participate. In this way, you will also probably get a closer relation to the professors compared to in Denmark.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:

questions.answer: A lot of more expensive travel days than I expected, but that was entirely my decision (haha),

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything was kind of expensive in Boston.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of clubs. I joined a soccer club and we started a running club in the exchange group, but BU also has an official running club which I joined one time. Also, Fitrec has a lot of offers - also outdoor hikes etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: FitTreks - join some of Fitrec's outdoor activities!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Outside Boston:
Within a relatively short distance to Boston, I went to NYC, Cape Cod, Martha's Vineyard and Washington D.C. Further, I went on a FitTreks hike to New Hampshire. 

In Boston: 
Go to a sports game or the parks in the center.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Boston is known as a "European" city so there is no real culture shock.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the university clubs or talk to your classmates (even though they are not always so talkative in class).

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The frat parties were overwhelming and not for me (haha).

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The university sports culture was great!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Firstly, be excited—Boston is a fantastic place for your exchange experience. Secondly, be outgoing and join clubs and activities to make the most of your time and meet new people. Lastly, explore other places on the East Coast; there's a lot to see and do beyond Boston.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't buy the local transportation semester card. Buy the Charliecard when you are there - you will figure out how it works. Also, you can subscribe to Bluebikes to rent bikes - it's easy and cheap.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Classes are smaller than in DK, so I had to participate a lot while my English was not that good.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
